name: Ace Hotel New York
why_included: Classic laptop lobby: big communal table plus lounge seating, free Wi-Fi, Stumptown up front; noisy, dim, outlets spotty. Group-friendly. Buying a drink is customary.

name: PUBLIC Hotel
why_included: Two lobby levels with workstations, nooks, big tables, couches; cafe on site. Laptops away after 6pm per house rules. Coffee purchase suggested. Group tables.

name: The Ludlow Hotel
why_included: Living-room lobby with fireplace and leather sofas; locals welcome on Wi-Fi. Calm, small; no purchase stated.

name: The Marlton Hotel
why_included: Wood-paneled lobby with espresso bar, fireplace, communal table; freelancers welcome. Coffee purchase customary; outlets limited.

name: The High Line Hotel
why_included: Coffee-shop-feel lobby with espresso bar; guests and non-guests work on banquettes, sofas and courtyard. Coffee purchase expected for courtyard.

name: Arlo SoHo
why_included: Library lounge with hidden outlets and 10-seat table, fiber Wi-Fi, lobby open 24h, grab-and-go cafe. Group table.

name: Arlo NoMad
why_included: Second-floor library work area with two long tables plus couches; fast Wi-Fi with email sign-in. Fills early. Group tables.

name: citizenM New York Times Square
why_included: Roomy design lobby with communal tables, free Wi-Fi, 24h canteenM cafe. Verify non-guest policy (Bowery branch reportedly charged). Group tables.

name: Dream Midtown (The Rickey)
why_included: The Rickey lounge: fast Wi-Fi, complimentary coffee/tea, food from Serafina; holds small groups by day. Ordering food/drink customary.

name: Hotel Indigo Lower East Side
why_included: 14th-floor lobby with skyline views, communal tables and charging stations; non-guests can use tables and couches. Group tables.

name: Kimpton Hotel Eventi
why_included: Living Room behind the lobby with fireplace, Wi-Fi, outlets; no reservation needed to work. Bar nearby; outdoor plaza in good weather.

name: The Beekman, a Thompson Hotel
why_included: Nine-story atrium lobby with coffee shop, solid Wi-Fi, quiet; non-guests can work without a stay. Some photo-taking foot traffic.

name: 11 Howard
why_included: Quiet second-floor Library open 7am-11pm serving coffee, tea and cocktails; strong Wi-Fi; good for writing and calls. Purchase likely expected.

name: The New York EDITION
why_included: Lobby Bar overlooking Madison Square Park with strong Wi-Fi, drinks and light bites; locals gather there. Ordering expected; upscale.

name: Moxy NYC Downtown (Recreation)
why_included: Third-floor lounge with 12-seat long table, couches, plentiful outlets, open Wi-Fi; can be loud. Group-friendly. Food, coffee and bar on site.

name: The Roxy Hotel
why_included: Local tip (Dec 2024): quiet lobby, good Wi-Fi, bathrooms; optional food from on-site coffee bar or hotel.

name: Ace Hotel Brooklyn
why_included: Lobby with large communal table, garden room, many outlets, free Wi-Fi; becomes a lounge at night. Buying a coffee suggested. Group table.

name: The Hoxton Williamsburg
why_included: Large lobby with vintage sofas, armchairs, two fireplaces; staff relaxed about people staying. Busy with freelancers; bar crowd later.

name: Moxy Brooklyn Williamsburg
why_included: Time Out (May 2025): lobby great for computer work, free all-day Wi-Fi, complimentary coffee 7-10am.

name: 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge
why_included: Plant-filled high-ceiling lobby lounge with couches and big windows; Neighbors cafe off lobby, coffee purchase implied. Quiet on weekday mornings.

name: Boro Hotel
why_included: LIC's best work lobby per Time Out: natural light, tables, sofas, free Wi-Fi; non-guests buy coffee or drinks at cafe-bar.

name: ICP Cafe (International Center of Photography)
why_included: Ground-floor cafe in ICP's free public space: free Wi-Fi, laptop plug-in stations, ample seating. Free Incubator Space too. Museum hours only.

name: Brookfield Place (Winter Garden & upper level)
why_included: Free mall seating: quiet cushy chairs upstairs, Winter Garden views near Hudson Eats; no purchase needed. Few or no outlets. Group seating.

name: Industry City common areas
why_included: Official FAQ: day visitors welcome to use common lobby spaces and courtyards; food hall on campus; building hours roughly 8am-10pm. Group-friendly.

name: David Rubenstein Atrium at Lincoln Center
address_hint: Broadway between W 62nd and W 63rd St
why_included: Free public atrium with movable tables, free Wi-Fi, food counter; many laptop users. Limited seating; busy Thursday free performances.

name: PAC NYC lobby (Perelman Performing Arts Center)
why_included: Lobby free and open to public 8am-11pm daily with restaurant/bar; suggested by locals as a work spot. Laptop policy unconfirmed.

name: Whole Foods Market Union Square (upstairs seating)
why_included: Large upstairs dining area overlooking the park; people work for hours. Customer seating: receipts may be checked when busy.

name: Whole Foods Market Tribeca (upstairs cafe)
why_included: Upstairs cafe open 7am-10pm with some outlets and quiet north-window seats; can be loud. Buy a snack.

name: Barnes & Noble Union Square Cafe
why_included: NYU News (Mar 2025): gigantic tables, wall outlets, free Wi-Fi; no purchase required. Good for group projects.

name: Capital One Cafe Union Square
why_included: Free to sit, no purchase required; most outlets of any spot in NYU's list, free Wi-Fi, multiple floors, booths. Crowded Sundays.

name: The Center for Fiction Cafe
why_included: Public bookstore cafe-bar: four 8-seat community tables, Wi-Fi with purchase (3h limit), few outlets, can be noisy. Group-friendly.
